method: Adversarial re-verification in the Higgsfield sandbox (open internet): Commons API (extmetadata, wikitext, revisions, upload log, categories, templates, user contribs); blobless git clones of pfnet-research/tgan, pfnet-research/tgan2, songweige/TATS, snap-research/MoCoGAN-HD, THUDM/CogVideo (LICENSE text, tree at pinned commit, git log of each asset, commit authors, later LICENSE/README changes); full download of every media_url (curl -sIL plus body download, sha256, PIL/ffprobe frame counts, durations, dimensions); arXiv abs pages of every cited version (licence link), arXiv API (dates, abstracts), arXiv PDFs v1/v2/v4 (caption text and page numbers via pdftotext), e-print tarballs (TeX captions, figure PDFs via pdfimages/pdftotext); Internet Archive metadata API; Hacker News thread for the IA clip's origin. LIMITATION: no frame of any clip was viewed by this verifier (no vision path from the sandbox; a Higgsfield video_analysis upload was attempted and was blocked by the permission classifier, so it was NOT done). Every statement about visual content is inherited from page text or measured; every kept GIF/still therefore carries a mandatory human visual review condition.

conditions: Credit on screen and in the description: 'Zisaac33, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons' plus the file-page URL and the licence link https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0 (CC BY-SA 4.0 requires attribution, licence link and an indication of changes).

Indicate changes (crop, retime, overlays, transcode). Format-shifting alone is a technical modification permitted by CC 4.0 s.2(a)(4); any crop, retime or annotation makes the excerpt Adapted Material, so ShareAlike (BY-SA 4.0 or compatible) attaches to that adapted excerpt. It need not attach to the whole film if the clip stays a distinct component, but get legal sign-off before compositing these pixels into graphics that will not be BY-SA.
Label honestly on screen: 'DCGAN (2015 image GAN), 2021 hobbyist training run, image grid - not a video model'. Never present it as historical video-generation footage or as a text-to-video result.
